question: Two friends each roll a die in secret. You ask whether either rolled a six; they say yes. Chance both did?
answer: 1 in 11. Of the 36 equally likely pairs, 11 contain at least one six, and only one of those is a double six. The yes ruled out the 25 pairs without a six, but it did not tell you which die showed it, so the other die is not a fresh roll.
move: Ask exactly what you were told, and which cases it rules out.
trap: One die shows a six, so the other feels like a fresh roll.

diagram.label: equally likely pairs
diagram.caption: The yes leaves 11 pairs, and only one of them is a double six.

reference: Feller, An Introduction to Probability Theory and Its Applications, Volume 1, Wiley, 1968
